brief.product: Specimen tracking for a hospital pathology lab. Technicians scan a specimen in at receiving and follow it through processing, staining and reporting, all shift, on wall-mounted screens in the lab.
brief.notes: Every specimen carries an accession number and a block number, and both appear on nearly every row. Screens are read from a metre away under bright light. A rejected or contaminated specimen must be impossible to miss, and must never be confused with one that is merely waiting.

accent.why: A deep indigo sits far from the red used for rejected specimens and the green used for success, so under bright light a primary action is never mistaken for a status.

temperature.why: Specimen tracking in a hospital lab is technical work read against bright light, and a true grey keeps the status colours clean and unambiguous.

pairing.why: Accession and block numbers are read from a metre away on every row, so Atkinson Hyperlegible for the text and Spline Sans Mono for the codes puts legibility above character.

radius.why: Rows of accession and block numbers are dense data, and sharp corners suit that technical table work.

density.why: The technicians are trained staff on shift all day, but the screens are wall-mounted and read from a metre away, so taller rows and wider gaps help scanning at distance.

motif.why: Every row carries an accession number and a block number, so a mono uppercase label above titles and stat tiles makes reference codes the visible habit of the app.

copy.headline: Every specimen, from receiving to report.
copy.tagline: Scan it in, follow it through processing, staining and reporting, and know where it stands.
copy.why: The copy names the lab's actual path for a specimen and what a technician came to do, with nothing about software.
